questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A quadrilateral has four equal sides and four right angles. What is the most specific name for it?
questions.why: A rectangle only needs right angles, and a rhombus only needs equal sides — a shape with BOTH four equal sides and four right angles must be a square, the most specific name.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: A historian writes 'poor harvests caused food shortages, which led to rising anger at the government.' Which part of this is the consequence, not the cause?
questions.why: The consequence is the result that follows from the cause. Poor harvests (cause) led to shortages, which led to anger (the consequence) — students often mix up which event is doing the causing.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle is 110°. What is the co-interior (allied) angle on the other parallel line?
questions.why: Co-interior angles between parallel lines add up to 180°, so 180° − 110° = 70°. A common mistake is treating them as equal like corresponding angles instead of supplementary.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: During the Crusades, which group controlled Jerusalem before the First Crusade began in 1096?
questions.why: Jerusalem was under Muslim control when Pope Urban II called for the First Crusade, prompting European Christians to try to capture the city — this is why the crusades began.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: During a flood investigation, which factor is a NATURAL cause of increased flood risk, rather than a human one?
questions.why: Heavy rainfall is a natural trigger of flooding, while deforestation, concrete surfaces, and floodplain building are human factors that worsen flood risk — students often lump all causes together without distinguishing natural from human.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Magna Carta, signed in 1215, is significant mainly because it established which principle?
options: The king must obey the law like everyone else
The king should choose all bishops himself
England should have no king at all
questions.answer: The king must obey the law like everyone else
questions.why: Magna Carta was revolutionary because it limited royal power by placing the king under the law, not above it — a common misconception is that it abolished monarchy entirely, which it did not.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: A student tests whether the amount of sleep (hours per night) affects test scores. They keep the difficulty of the test the same for everyone. What is the controlled variable?
questions.why: The controlled variable is what is kept the SAME so it doesn't affect results. Hours of sleep is the independent variable (what's changed) and test scores is the dependent variable (what's measured) — mixing these up is the chronic error.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A triangle has one angle of 90° and two equal sides. What type of triangle is it?
questions.why: A triangle can be classified by both its angles and its sides at once — here it has a right angle (right-angled) and two equal sides (isosceles), so both terms apply together.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Solve for x: 3(x + 2) − 5 = 13. A student says 'I'll just subtract 2 from both sides first since it's inside the bracket.' Explain in one sentence why that's wrong, then give x.
options: You must expand the bracket first — x = 4
You can subtract 2 first since brackets don't matter — x = 4
You must expand the bracket first — x = 6
You can subtract 2 first since brackets don't matter — x = 6
questions.answer: You must expand the bracket first — x = 4
questions.why: The 2 inside the bracket is multiplied by 3, not just added, so you can't remove it directly. Expanding gives 3x + 6 − 5 = 13, so 3x + 1 = 13, 3x = 12, x = 4.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes a long-term cause from a short-term (trigger) cause of an event?
options: A long-term cause builds up over years; a short-term cause is the immediate spark that sets off the event
A long-term cause and short-term cause are always the same thing
A long-term cause happens after the event; a short-term cause happens before
A short-term cause is always more important than a long-term cause
questions.answer: A long-term cause builds up over years; a short-term cause is the immediate spark that sets off the event
questions.why: Long-term causes create the underlying conditions for an event over time, while short-term causes are the immediate trigger — students often think the trigger is the ONLY cause, ignoring the deeper build-up.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: Your friend says 'the independent variable is whatever changes during the experiment, so it must be the dependent variable too, since that also changes.' Using an example of your own (not sleep, sunlight, fertiliser, water temperature, or soil type), explain why the independent and dependent variables are NOT the same thing, and describe what makes each one distinct.
